population: Explicitly nonclinical eligible adult (18+) recreational novice-to-experienced hybrid runners/strength trainees in V1; offline synthetic Node24 reference only. No elite, adolescent, pregnancy/postpartum, frailty, rehabilitation or clinical-clearance extrapolation.
authoritySplit: Sports science approves these reusable envelopes, relationships and operational ranges. Coaching Intelligence composes and selects concrete sessions inside them with a traceable reason. A concrete generated workout inside an approved envelope needs no paper of its own; out-of-envelope output fails closed.
principles: A first program starts from onboarding-like facts. Unknown capacity is resolved by conservative establishment and observation, never by demanding a perfect prior week and never by inventing a dose.

The first week never exceeds the athlete's current reported running exposure; missing exposure is not poor tolerance and not proof of tolerance. When current exposure is zero or unknown, only the walk/jog ladder (step 0) and the reviewed 15-20 minute easy entry are used.

Future weeks show a planned trajectory. Every planned step is conditional: it advances only after the previous comparable exposure was executed without an adverse signal; otherwise the dose repeats, and repeated adverse response regresses one step. Nothing progresses from elapsed calendar time: quality and strides activation, set increases at block boundaries and ladder steps count executed weeks.

Chosen days and shifts are hard agenda constraints. Each chosen day carries a session of that sport when a supported session exists; otherwise it carries an explained lower-demand option (walk, mobility, rest by design) and the conflict is negotiated, never silently moved or dropped. More days spread weekly load; they never add to it.

Contextual priority is derived from goals, event and phase, never from a required static priority flag. Arrangement trade-offs are resolved Pareto-first, then by the lowest worst-case joint harm across H0 session, H1 week, H2 block and H3 goal; a genuinely incomparable trade-off is asked, not hidden behind candidate order.

Running intensity comes from current effort anchors (talk test and perceived effort). An aspirational time goal or easy pace never defines training pace. The first exposure to a new intensity family is a calibration that observes pace and response.
Strength loads come from known current loads or from effort-guided establishment inside the first exposure. Sex, body size and other exercises never supply an individual load.
Strength remains present across event phases at a reduced dose; it does not disappear automatically.

Return after a nonclinical interruption uses current evidence as the starting point and prior tolerance as the ceiling. There is no universal percentage rollback. Clinical or unknown-cause interruptions never receive a nonclinical return recipe.

Partial, missing, duplicate, stale, corrected or conflicting observations keep their provenance and uncertainty. One event never creates a rule; missing data is never negative evidence; duplicates never double-count training.
All numeric values below are operational coaching choices inside reviewed envelopes. They are not physiological laws, injury-prevention thresholds or predictions of individual response.

R6-COLD-START.claim: An eligible adult with no product history can receive a complete conditional first program built from onboarding-like facts, with establishment sessions wherever capacity is unknown.
requires: current nonclinical eligibility (unknown is ASK, clinical routes to a human)
chosen days and time per session for each programmed sport
limits: no fitness test, maximal effort or race-pace estimate in week 1
no injury-prevention claim
no universal starter dose beyond the listed establishment entries

R6-LOAD-ESTABLISHMENT.claim: An unknown external load is resolved inside the first loaded exposure by technique practice and an ascending ramp: start with the lightest available load and add the smallest increment between preparatory sets while at least the target repetitions in reserve remain with stable technique; the working load is the heaviest such load, recorded with its convention.
limits: no kilogram from sex, body mass, another exercise or another implement
RIR is approximate; technique and comfort govern continuation
novices practice unloaded or with a light implement before any effort-guided loading

R6-PLANNED-PROGRESSION.claim: A planned, response-gated trajectory with one progression dimension per session type per step, small absolute steps and periodic consolidation weeks is a defensible recreational progression model.
limits: no ten-percent or other universal injury rule is claimed
planned future doses are conditional proposals, not predictions
no progression from elapsed calendar alone

R6-RUN-QUALITY.claim: Recreational runners with established current easy running can be introduced to relaxed strides and to effort-anchored controlled-hard (threshold/cruise) work, and event-specific work later, with volume progressed by repetitions or duration at stable effort.
limits: not for walk/jog establishment or the first two established weeks
at most one quality session per week
never on the day before or after the long run when another chosen run day can hold it
no VO2max/threshold pace prediction, no pace from goal time or easy pace
hills only when terrain is declared

R6-HYBRID-ARRANGEMENT.claim: Residual-fatigue interactions between sessions differ by direction and gap: heavy lower-body resistance work within roughly the preceding day can impair a key run more than a controlled run impairs next-day strength; same-session order matters most; upper-body work interacts little with running.
limits: ordinal classes only, never summed into a score
individual athlete evidence may override the population ordering
self-reported tolerated arrangements stay admissible
An arrangement whose own combined response is unknown stays admissible with disclosed uncertainty when current whole-week tolerance covers the same tasks; adverse arrangement evidence excludes it

R6-SUBSTITUTION.claim: When equipment or circumstance removes an exercise, a same-pattern substitute that preserves movement intent may replace it; an unfamiliar substitute starts with effort-guided establishment and the stimulus change is disclosed.
limits: no load conversion between exercises or implements
no claim that bodyweight practice equals external-load strength
no progression while changing the task

R6-NONCLINICAL-RETURN.claim: After a known nonclinical interruption with current ordinary function, re-entry starts from current evidence (a current demonstration or the R4 entry) and returns to the prior tolerated dose in conditional steps, scaled by interruption length.
limits: no universal percentage rollback
historical maxima are a ceiling, not current proof
illness, pain, injury or unknown cause never receive this recipe

R6-EVENT-TRANSITION.claim: For recreational 10K and half-marathon events, a progressive volume reduction over the final one to two weeks while maintaining session frequency and a short intensity touch, with strength kept at a reduced dose and stopped in the final days, followed by an easy nonclinical post-event week, is a defensible event transition.
limits: no finish-time guarantee or readiness claim
no new intensity, overload or new exercise in the taper
no fixed universal recovery day count after the race; function and eligibility are checked

R6-PARTIAL-NOISY-LEARNING.claim: Imperfect real-world observations can inform near-term coaching (hold, advance, regress, rank) when provenance, comparability, recency, consistency and hysteresis are kept, without causal or physiological claims.
limits: partial work informs only the observed component and adherence
missing effort or heart rate is unknown, not adverse
duplicates merge, conflicts quarantine, stale data expires

Build-phase labels (foundation, development, specific, consolidation) are operational partitions: observations of the identical prescription and arrangement stay comparable across them; taper, race week, post-event and return phases never pool with build phases

R6-ROTATION.claim: Exercise rotation can follow the athlete's preference by changing accessories and close variants while main lifts stay, deferring any change near an event and establishing each new exercise by effort.
limits: FIXED keeps the selection except needed substitutions
rotation never transfers load and never coincides with a progression step on the new exercise

establishment.notes: When current exposure is zero or unknown, only walkJogLadder step 0 and the unknownExposureEasyMinutes entry are used; load-establishment rows appear only when R6-LOAD-ESTABLISHMENT is enabled.
establishment.belowMinimumSession: Current running below run.minimumSessionMinutes (longest current run or weekly running) cannot hold a continuous easy run: the athlete starts on the walk/jog ladder. A non-novice starts at the highest ladder step whose jogging per session is within both the longest current run and current weekly running divided by the walk/jog exposures of the week (maxWalkJogDaysPerWeek at most); novices and zero or unknown exposure start at step 0 (SSCTR D42).

strides.optionalNote: For EASY_LOW or novice runners strides are optional; the easy run without them is an equal alternative.

effortCues.EASY_CONVERSATIONAL: Conversational effort (about 2-4 of 10): full sentences are possible; walk breaks are allowed
effortCues.STRIDE_RELAXED_FAST: Relaxed fast strides (about 7 of 10): smooth and controlled, never a sprint
effortCues.THRESHOLD_CONTROLLED: Comfortably hard and controlled (about 6-7 of 10): short phrases only; you could hold it much longer than the repetition
effortCues.TEN_K_EFFORT: Hard but controlled (about 7-8 of 10): a few words at a time; finish every repetition with form intact

singleRunCeiling.appliesTo: Every planned run except the race, including long-run steps, RESTART->EASY and WALK_JOG->EASY transitions and return steps
singleRunCeiling.reference: Longest completed run in the preceding windowDays from the completed-work ledger; in a conditional projection, earlier projected weeks count as executed. Walk/jog sessions count their jogging minutes. With no completed run in the window, the reviewed entry (return.entryRunMinutes) is the ceiling in every week, not only the first projected week; in the first cold-start week the intake ceiling applies.
singleRunCeiling.disclosure: When the reference run is under 50 minutes a 5-minute step exceeds 10% of it; the step stays response-gated, is disclosed and is never combined with another single-session increase in the same week.

run.longRunShareSemantics: longRunShareOfWeeklyMinutesMax applies in every week with at least three running sessions (walks excluded). The cap holds the long run, it never shortens it: the long run is never reduced below the typical easy run of that week, nor below the long run prescribed in the last build week (a shorter quality session on the ladder does not shorten the long run).
run.earned: At most one step per progression dimension per week. EARNED may release a step the cadence would hold (easy-run cadence, load tick) or skip a consolidation hold, never more. Unavailable in WALK_JOG, RESTART and RETURN modes, where it counts as ADVANCE.
run.activationCounts: qualityRequiresEstablishedEasyWeeks and strides.requiresEstablishedEasyWeeks count executed non-establishment easy weeks (EASY and LONG gates ADVANCE or EARNED); stride repetitions add one every two further executed easy weeks.

strength.setIncreaseAtBlockBoundary: Per exercise, only when the final exposures of that exercise in the block were ADVANCE or EARNED, and never for a block in which the exercise had a return-entry or return-step exposure (SSCTR D49).
strength.resumeAfterDays: An exercise not performed for more than return.moderateMaxDays (rotation back, end of a substitution window) restarts with effort-guided establishment; its last logged load is a ceiling.
strength.loadUnits: Loads are kilograms inside the engine. A pound value (intake or log) is converted at the boundary to the nearest 0.5 kg and kept as reported; any other or missing unit, or a logged convention different from the planned one, leaves the load unknown: it is never adopted and the athlete is asked to confirm it. A reported known dose above six sets is kept as history and the plan starts at six.

loggedLoadAdoption.semantics: A logged load becomes the reference only inside 0 to maximumKilograms kg and at most maximumIncrementsAbovePlanned smallest increment above the load the plan stated for that exposure (the known load, or the last logged load for a from-log row). A load above the stated one is adopted only when that exposure met the ADVANCE criterion (target reps met, minimum logged RIR at or above the prescription minus gates.advanceMinimumLoggedRirBelowPrescribed, no adverse response); otherwise the planned load stays and the athlete is asked (SSCTR D44). A logged load is never adopted above a re-establishment ceiling or, during a return, above the load before the break: it is capped there and asked about. A first establishment log (no planned load, no ceiling, no earlier load) is not a number: the next exposure is from-log with no number, its instructions describe effort-guided selection only and never point to the logged value (SSCTR D48), and the athlete is asked. It becomes the reference only when the athlete confirms it (review loadConfirmations: exercise, value, unit kg or lb, the planned convention), when a second log of the same exercise (a later exposure, or an earlier one in the same week) agrees with it within establishmentAgreementIncrements smallest increment, or when it is within establishmentAgreementIncrements smallest increment of the athlete's own load hint in the same convention (SSCTR D45). A confirmation replaces the logged value and never bypasses the other rules. Anything else keeps the planned reference and is asked about. A known planned load replaced by a different executed load is a modification, not an instantiation. Numeric plausibility of a logged value inside the 0 to maximumKilograms bound, including a load logged far below the plan (SSCTR R5), belongs to Data and is an open gap.

strength.setsAfterReestablishment: After an exercise is re-established by effort, its earlier set count comes back one set per executed week, never at once.

event.runVolumeRangeSemantics: taperWeekRunVolumeRange, taperWeekLongRunRange and raceWeekRunVolumeRange are per-session fractions of the corresponding achieved (executed) peak session, not weekly totals.
event.taperQualitySemantics: taperQualityWorkRange applies to total work minutes (repetitions x work minutes) of the achieved peak quality session; repetition length is kept when fewer repetitions fit the range, otherwise repetitions shorten.
event.achievedPeakBasis: Taper and race-week doses derive from executed sessions; with no executed quality the taper and race week are easy-only, and with no executed strides the shakeout has none.
event.legacyRaceWeekQuality: A familiar quality task at least raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days before the race becomes the raceWeekTouch dose of the event (never more than the familiar task); closer to the race it is an easy run.
event.postRaceEligibility: A review on or after race day in RACE_WEEK or POST_EVENT, or before a NEXT_BLOCK week, needs an eligibility and function assessment dated on or after the race; otherwise ASK.
event.proximitySemantics: Event rules count days to the race, never calendar weeks. Every session 1 to raceWindowDays days before the race follows race-week rules (no long run and no quality session; an optional shakeout the day before; at most one race-effort touch on the run day closest to the race that is still at least raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days before it; other runs short and easy) and every session in the taper days before that (7 days per taper week) follows taper rules, whichever calendar week it falls in. Strength in the race window: none in the last raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days, and at most one short light session (raceWeekStrengthSets sets, main lifts only, at least raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir in reserve) on the strength day furthest from the race inside the window; strength on taper days takes the taper dose. Sessions after the race follow the post-event rules by days since the race.
event.raceDateUnavailable: A race date marked unavailable (event-week conflict or unavailable day) is asked about; the race is never kept or skipped silently.
event.modeAwareSessions: Taper, race-window and post-event sessions keep or reduce what the athlete has reached in the current run mode (SSCTR D43). Walk/jog: taper days hold the current ladder step, race-window days use one step back, the day before the race is an optional walk, post-event days are optional walk/jog one step back. Restart or return: taper days hold the current easy minutes, race-window days take raceWeekRunVolumeRange of them (never below return.entryRunMinutes), the day before is an optional short easy run, post-event runs never exceed the current minutes. No touch, quality or strides for these modes. Walk/jog and restart steps do not advance on taper, race-window or post-event days; the next block starts the walk/jog ladder one step back. Warm-up strides on race day and strides in the shakeout appear only after strides were executed.

raceDayCompletion.semantics: Race day is a completion at conversational effort with walk breaks (no strides, no surges, nothing to press) when the run mode in race week is one of modes (walk/jog, restart or return); when the run mode in any earlier week of this program was one of historyModes (walk/jog or restart, from the starting class or applied by a review; the run state keeps this history through mode changes, reviews and reprojections; SSCTR D47); or for a half marathon whose achieved long run is below halfMarathonAchievedLongRunBelowMinutes (the LONG_RUN_PEAK_BELOW_TARGET material threshold; SSCTR D43 and R9). No other exemption applies: one for athletes who rebuild a substantial long run would have to be declared and reviewed first. Whenever race day is a completion, the program or the proposal carries the non-blocking EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING negotiation with both options (keep the event and complete it with walk breaks; a later or shorter event), recomputed from the race-week state of every proposal. It states the longest continuous run executed by race week: the longest executed easy, long, restart or return run or ladder step without walk breaks, never 0 when such a run was reached (a restart after a long interruption starts this count again). In walk/jog it states the ladder step as well; in a return in race week it states the current easy minutes instead. It also states why race day is a completion: the run mode in race week, the program history or the half-marathon long run.

event.longRunFloor: In taper weeks and at the start of the next block the long run is never shorter than that week's easy run (SSCTR R10).

return.reasonScreen: A nonclinical break needs a structured nonclinical reason category (in the legacy R5 contract, clinicalReason=false is that structured answer); free text alone never confirms one and the category is asked. Free text in English, Portuguese and Spanish can only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes: it is split into clauses at punctuation, dashes, slashes and but/mas/pero; an explicit denial ("no pain", "nothing clinical", "didn't feel any pain", "não senti dor", "no tuve dolor") covers the clinical words it governs and further ones joined only by or/nor (ou/nem, o/ni), and is honoured only when no earlier negation or inability word in the same clause makes it an affirmation ("couldn't run without pain" names pain); a without/sem/sin denial counts only at the start of its clause and is asked about elsewhere ("it was hard to run without pain"). No denial counts in a clause that also carries a time or contrast condition (until, before, after, except, unless, only when; até, antes, depois, exceto, salvo, só quando; hasta, antes, después, excepto, salvo, solo cuando): it is asked about ("didn't feel any pain until I ran"). The clinical lexicon covers common medical conditions, procedures, treatments and symptoms in the three languages (for example heart attack, stroke, cancer, chemotherapy, fracture, hernia, kidney stones, dengue, nausea, headache, bleeding, stitches, dislocation, panic attack, high blood pressure), and a damage verb with a body part in the same clause is a clinical mention ("broke my leg", "quebrei a perna", "me rompí la pierna"); body parts alone and words such as sore, cramps, anxiety or treatment are ambiguous. Any clinical category or mention routes to CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED regardless of nonclinical flags; ambiguous words (body parts, fatigue, not feeling well, falls in all three languages) and unrecognized or missing reasons are ASK. Round-7 additions (SSCTR R7): birth and road or animal accident phrases (had a baby, tive um bebê, tuve un bebé, hit by a car, car crash, bike crash, car accident) and words (parto, atropelado/atropelada, atropellado/atropellada, bitten, mordida/mordido, mordedura) are clinical mentions; baby, bebê, crash, crashed, collision, bite, slipped, escorreguei/escorregou and resbalé/resbaló are ambiguous. A damage statement whose every damage verb is locally negated (the nearest word before the verb, past articles, possessives, clitics, auxiliaries and body parts, is a negation: "No broken bones", "Didn't break my leg", "Não quebrei a perna") is asked about instead of named clinical; a negation elsewhere in the clause does not hide it ("couldn't run because I broke my leg" stays clinical). The same screen applies to the intake pause and the legacy path. Round-8 additions (SSCTR R11): birth and pregnancy-loss words (cesarean, caesarean, C-section, cesariana, cesarea, miscarriage, aborto) and procedures (vasectomy, colonoscopy, endoscopy, LASIK, root canal; vasectomia, colonoscopia, endoscopia, tratamento de canal, endodoncia) are clinical mentions; maternity, newborn and breastfeeding words (maternity, maternidade, maternidad, newborn, recem-nascido, recien nacido, breastfeeding, amamentando, amamentacao, lactancia, amamantando), assault words (assault, assaulted, mugged, beaten, agredido, agredida, agressao, agresion, assaltado, asaltado), stings (stung, sting, picada, picadura, ferroada) and bruises (bruise, bruised, bruising, hematoma) are ambiguous; burned, burnt, cut, queimei, queimou, cortei, cortou, queme and corte are damage verbs; hand, hands, thumb, nose, eye, eyes and face, with mao, maos, polegar, nariz, olho, olhos, rosto, mano, manos, pulgar, ojo and ojos, are body parts; C-section and recem-nascido written with a hyphen or a space are joined before the clause split. Asking pregnancy and postpartum status again at reviews and returns belongs to the structured intake design (an open gap).

requires: observed after the interruption began and within currentDemonstrationMaxAgeDays
demonstration.minimumDuration: A demonstration shorter than run.minimumSessionMinutes demonstrates no easy-run capacity and is not used.

return.strengthKnownLoadAfterReturnLog: The prior KNOWN load is prescribed only after a post-interruption logged entry supports it; otherwise FROM_LOG from the entry log with the prior load as a ceiling.
return.interruptionFacts: Interruption days must be a whole number from 1 to 3650; start and end dates real dates with the start not after the end and neither after the review; days and dates that disagree by more than one day are a contradiction. Anything else is asked, never resolved to the least conservative class. A clinical flag that means yes in any form (true, 1, yes, sim, sí) routes to a human; one that is neither yes nor no is asked.
return.eligibilityFlags: A clinical eligibility flag (pain, persistentPain, injury, illness, functionalLimitation, clinicalConcern) that means yes in any form (true, 1, yes, y, sim, si or sí; trimmed, letter case and accents ignored) routes to CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED in the intake, the review and the legacy R5 path, and so does a clinical eligibility status in any letter case. Any other non-boolean value leaves eligibility unassessed and is asked: unknown is neither clearance nor illness (SSCTR R6).
return.strengthEntryWeek: Every strength exposure in a return-entry week is at the entry dose (strengthEntrySets at strengthEntryMinimumRir or more reps in reserve), including a later exposure in that week of an exercise first set up in it; an exercise first set up in a return-entry week then follows the return steps like the others (author-found in R6-POLICY-4).
return.strengthReturnSets: Strength sets in a moderate or long return (SSCTR D49). The entry is strengthEntrySets at strengthEntryMinimumRir or more reps in reserve. Return step 2 is one set above the entry and at least one below the ceiling: max(1, min(ceiling - 1, strengthEntrySets + 1)) sets at 3 reps in reserve. The ceiling is the last set count executed before the break outside a return step and outside a phase reduction; without one, the known count; without that, the normal count. After the return steps the count comes back at most one set per executed week without a phase reduction, up to the ceiling (a step 2 reduced by its phase is followed by the step-2 count itself). It goes above the ceiling only through a development block completed with no return-step exposure of that exercise: each such block lifts the ceiling by one, still at most one set per executed week. Consolidation, specific, taper, race-week and post-event reductions apply on top, in the return steps too. Return-entry and return-step exposures never count toward a block-boundary set increase, and the block in progress at the break earns no set.
return.returnLoadCap: During the return steps a logged load is capped at the current return reference and asked about: the load before the break until an entry log is adopted, then the adopted entry load (no increase in step 2). After the return steps the usual adoption rules apply (SSCTR D45, Q3 and D49).
return.restartRunHistory: A restart after a long interruption starts the run history again: the achieved long, easy, quality and strides peaks and the longest continuous run are cleared, so the race-day statement and the taper, race-week, race-day and next-block doses come only from runs executed after the restart. A moderate return keeps them, since it returns to the prior dose (author-found with SSCTR D47).

pooling.arrangementPreferenceQuery: sessionType + phaseClass + doseKey (quality family, ladder and step of the current quality session); no query without a current quality dose

learning.missingGate: A run dimension or exercise with no executed session in the reviewed week has no gate and holds; in a conditional projection a run dimension advances only when the week plans a session of it (SSCTR D46), and restart and return sessions of any role gate on EASY there, as in reviews (SSCTR R13). Such a dimension never counts as an executed week, never unlocks quality or strides and never converts a walk. A week with no easy run planned (every easy day a walk) uses the executed long run for the development-week count and the walk conversion instead; the first converted walk becomes an easy run at run.minimumSessionMinutes that then progresses like the others (SSCTR R12).
learning.conflicts: A report that conflicts with another for the same session (same event id with different facts, different physical facts or responses, or one wearable activity bound to two sessions) stays in the completed-work record, flagged, and is quarantined: the session is CONFLICTED for gating and the facts count for neither capacity nor learning until a correction resolves them. A report dated before the activity it reports is rejected.
learning.consentScope: Without learning consent the athlete model stays empty and no athlete-specific pattern (learned rearrangement or learned preference) changes the plan; gating on the plan’s own completed-work record does not depend on learning consent.

rotation.notes: Main lifts stay; accessories rotate on the cadence; close variants of main lifts are not rotated in R6. A rotated exercise starts with effort-guided establishment with no load transferred; a rotated-back exercise unused for more than return.moderateMaxDays restarts effort-guided with its last logged load as a ceiling.

hybridSemantics.anyRunBeforeLowerStrengthSameSession: An easy run within sameSessionGapHours before MODERATE or HEAVY lower-body work carries a LOW strength-axis cost when strength has a development role.
hybridSemantics.ranking: Pareto first; then leximax of the sorted severity multiset (worst first) per horizon under the phase lead; counts or sums are never used.
hybridSemantics.equalCostOrder: When options differ only in back-to-back order and carry identical costs, the order is disclosed as either; the default shows the longer planned session first. No tie-break depends on candidate identifiers.
hybridSemantics.sameDayLabel: Pairs on the same calendar day beyond sameSessionGapHours are labelled "earlier the same day".
hybridSemantics.unknownArrangementResponse: Admissible only with current whole-week tolerance for the same task set and frequency, worst H0 severity <= LOW and no same-day pairing absent from the athlete reported routine; otherwise arrangement evidence or ASK. In the cold-start path every same-day pairing comes from the athlete own chosen days and shifts.
hybridSemantics.disclosure: A selected arrangement that keeps a MODERATE or higher cost is disclosed to the athlete with the alternatives (keep, swap shifts, move one session to another chosen day), at cold start and after any re-arrangement.

knownLimits: No measured threshold, VO2max, heart-rate zone or pace prediction
Hills only with declared terrain; no hill dose from flat pace
No marathon, ultra, triathlon or elite programming
No clinical return, rehabilitation, pregnancy/postpartum or adolescent programming
No guaranteed finish time, readiness or fitness gain
No universal hybrid maintenance minimum; strength reductions near events are operational choices inside the envelope
revisionNote: R6-POLICY-2 answers the SSCTR review of R6-POLICY-1 (hash 81114d89...): it declares values that were hard-coded, states the semantics the review asked for and tightens wording. Envelope claims are unchanged except where the review required new wording. R6-POLICY-3 (2026-10-26): declarations for the FREEZE-2 fixes of the independent engineering review of FREEZE-1 (QRE-R6-01…23): event proximity by days to the race, walk/jog below the minimum session, the single-run ceiling in every projected week, load units and logged-load adoption, sets after re-establishment, gates without evidence, conflicts and append-only record, learning-consent scope, interruption facts and the widened free-text screen. No envelope magnitude is widened. R6-POLICY-4 (2026-10-26): SSCTR round-7 defects D42 (walk/jog start within the longest current run), D43 (mode-aware event sessions and completion race day, with R9), D46 (projection holds dimensions without a planned session) and recommendation R10 (long-run floor). It also answers D44 (an above-plan logged load only on the ADVANCE criterion), D45 (an establishment log stays pending until it is confirmed, repeated or matches the athlete's own hint; review loadConfirmations; the return-entry ceiling), recommendations R6 (yes-meaning eligibility flags) and R7 (round-7 lexical residuals; locally negated damage is asked), and one author-found return-entry defect (every exposure of the entry week at the entry dose; exercises first set up in it follow the return steps). The logged-load bounds are now read from loggedLoadAdoption. No envelope magnitude is widened. R6-POLICY-5 (2026-10-26): SSCTR round-8 defects D47 (race day is a completion, with its negotiation, also when the program used walk/jog or restart in any week before the race, from the start or applied by a review; the negotiation states the longest continuous run executed by race week), D48 (a row whose load waits for confirmation instructs effort-guided selection only) and D49 (return weeks earn no block-boundary set; return step 2 and the following weeks come back from the last executed set count before the break, at most one set per executed week, with phase reductions on top; the return load cap as the runtime applies it), one author-found change (a restart after a long interruption clears the achieved run peaks, so the taper and race week come only from runs executed after it), and recommendations R11 (round-8 lexical residuals), R12 (with no easy run planned, the executed long run gates the walk conversion) and R13 (restart and return sessions gate on EASY in projection). No envelope magnitude is widened.
